headline: GOLD EYES $4,448 BREAKOUT AS RATE-HIKE BETS FADE — Metal Technically Bullish Above $4,333 After Warsh Selloff; September Hike Odds Slide From 66% Peak
snippet: Gold is rebounding from its post-Jackson Hole selloff as Fed rate-hike odds ease from a 66% peak toward 55%, with the metal holding above the $4,333 technical support level that analysts say defines the current bull structure. A clean break above $4,448 would open the path toward $4,518, with silver stabilizing after its 2.77% September 1 drop. The FXEmpire technical analysis notes that as long as gold holds $4,333, the medium-term uptrend remains intact — and that the market's post-Warsh repricing may be overblown given the structural drivers (central bank buying, debasement trade, institutional underweight in miners) that have not changed. September 4 payrolls will be the next directional trigger.

headline: PECOY DRILLS 804 METRES AT 0.34% COPPER IN PERU — Plus 42.3m At 1.01% Cu Near Surface As Third Kilometre-Scale Breccia Intercept Expands System
snippet: Pecoy Copper Corp. (TSX-V: PCU) announced September 1 its third consecutive kilometre-scale copper intercept in the South Breccia zone at its Pecoy Copper-Gold-Molybdenum-Silver Project in southern Peru: hole PEC26-072 returned 804.0 metres grading 0.34% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au from 24.0 metres depth, including 485.2 metres at 0.40% Cu and a high-grade subzone of 100.8 metres at 0.56% Cu from 608.5 metres. The separate Northwest target returned 42.3 metres at 1.01% Cu near surface. Three consecutive kilometre-scale bulk-tonnage intercepts from shallow depth at $6.60+/lb copper is the definition of a district-scale system in one of the world's most copper-endowed jurisdictions — the South Breccia remains open at depth and strike, and the fully funded 35,000m 2026 program is just getting started.

headline: AZZURO RED HILL VMS: 2m AT 11.95% COPPER IN MONGOLIA — Final 2026 Assays Confirm 550m Strike; 15–30Mt Exploration Target Open At Depth
snippet: Azzuro Resources (ASX: AZ9) released its final 2026 drill batch September 1, confirming high-grade copper-gold VMS mineralisation across approximately 550 metres of strike at the Red Hill project in Mongolia: hole MU2610A returned 5.0 metres at 4.92% Cu, 0.94 g/t Au, and 5.05 g/t Ag from 142.5 metres, including 2.0 metres at 11.95% Cu, 1.99 g/t Au — grades that rank among the best in any active ASX copper discovery program. A new zone of copper mineralisation was also intersected in MU2609 north of the shallow gold corridor. The project hosts a JORC 2012 exploration target of 15–30 million tonnes at 0.71–0.90% Cu and 0.26–0.40 g/t Au, remaining open to the east, west, and down-dip.

headline: TRIPLE MINE FAILURE LOCKS IN COPPER SUPPLY CRISIS — Grasberg Force Majeure, Codelco 20-Year Low, Kamoa Flooded; $6.59/lb Copper Holds Near Record
snippet: Crux Investor analysis documents why copper is holding near record levels above $6.59/lb ($14,500/tonne) despite some demand moderation: three of the world's four largest copper mines are simultaneously underperforming. Freeport's Grasberg (force majeure from the 2025 mudslide), Codelco (August output at a 20-year low, 1.34M-tonne target abandoned), and Kamoa-Kakula (Zijin warns flooding could cut its share by 57,000 tonnes) are all below plan. The analysis concludes: supply constraints alone — not speculative positioning — are now the primary price driver, and no new mine of scale reaches production before 2028. Junior copper developers in Athabasca, B.C., and the Americas continue to see capital inflows as the structural supply gap calcifies.

headline: SILVER'S 6TH DEFICIT YEAR NOW WORSE THAN EXPECTED — 46.3Moz Shortfall Up 15%; COMEX Stocks Collapsed 70% Since 2020 As China Controls Bite
snippet: Silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit has deepened beyond initial Silver Institute projections, with the 2026 shortfall now estimated at 46.3 million troy ounces — up 15% from 2025's 40.3 Moz gap. The cumulative draw since 2021 exceeds 762 million ounces from above-ground stocks. COMEX registered inventories have collapsed approximately 70% since 2020, while LBMA vaults have shed roughly 40% of their holdings. China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material — restricting exports to 44 licensed firms — removed a key Western refining input. Meanwhile, coin and bar demand is up 18% year-on-year, with retail investors accumulating at a pace consistent with previous bull market peaks. Industrial demand (solar, EVs, data centres, 5G) continues to absorb over 720 million ounces annually — a secular demand floor that the deficit arithmetic cannot accommodate from existing stocks much longer.

headline: FRIDAY PAYROLLS WILL DECIDE SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE — Gold Holds Technical Floor As Oil Above $90 And Elevated Yields Keep Hike Risk Alive
snippet: Gold is navigating a binary setup into September 4 payrolls: strong jobs data would reinforce Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole stance and likely push September rate hike probability back above 70%, pressuring gold through key support at $4,300; weak data would cut hike odds and potentially restart the bull move toward prior highs near $4,700. The complicating factor: oil above $90/bbl adds an inflation channel that could keep rate hike odds elevated even on a softer jobs print. For junior mining investors, the payrolls number this Friday is the single most important data point of the next six weeks — it sets the tone not just for September but for whether the Q4 seasonal rally starts from a higher or lower base.

headline: ECONOMY "RAPIDLY DETERIORATING" — Fed Will Inevitably Reverse; That Policy Pivot Will Be Jet Fuel For Precious Metals, Says GoldSeek
snippet: GoldSeek's latest market analysis argues that the Fed's September rate-hike posture is fundamentally at odds with a rapidly deteriorating economy, and that the central bank will be forced to reverse course before year-end — a policy pivot that would send gold, silver, and mining stocks significantly higher from current levels. The piece contends that Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks represent peak tightening rhetoric rather than a new policy ceiling: with credit stress rising, Treasury auction dynamics worsening, and employment data softening, the window for sustained restrictive policy is shorter than markets are currently pricing. The conclusion for mining investors: the post-Warsh selloff is an accumulation opportunity, not a trend reversal.

headline: GDX: GOLD STUNG BY HAWKISH WARSH, BUT MINERS REMAIN COMPELLING BUY — 10.4x P/E, 11.8% EPS Growth, $115 Technical Target After Post-Jackson Hole Selloff
snippet: A Seeking Alpha analysis of the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) argues that the post-Jackson Hole selloff in gold equities has created the best risk-reward entry since July, with GDX now trading at just 10.4x P/E against an 11.8% long-term earnings growth rate — a combination that implies severe undervaluation at $4,300+ gold. The technical picture shows GDX consolidating at a key support level with measured move targets to $115, representing approximately 15% upside from current levels. The fundamental backdrop is unchanged: major producers are generating record free cash flow at current gold prices while trading at multi-decade valuation discounts. The Warsh shock changed the near-term narrative, not the underlying business reality for gold miners.

headline: STARS ALIGNING FOR URANIUM: Kazatomprom Downflex + SMR Order Surge = Deepening Structural Deficit Through 2030
snippet: Sprott's updated uranium market analysis identifies a convergence of bullish catalysts entering September 2026: Kazatomprom's confirmed downflex of 2026 production by approximately 10% below its already-reduced 77 million pound guidance; Cameco mining below delivery commitments (14–16.5 Mlbs produced vs. 29–32 Mlbs contracted); and accelerating Small Modular Reactor orders from Microsoft and other tech majors expanding future reactor demand beyond IEA baseline forecasts. Sprott notes that uranium spot remains around $89–90/lb while long-term contract prices settled at $91.50 in Q1 2026 — an unusual configuration where term prices exceed spot, signalling that utilities are pricing future tightness into their procurement decisions today. For junior Athabasca Basin developers, this is the pricing environment that unlocks project economics.

headline: CHINA'S SOLAR RECORD IS A SILVER SUPPLY STORY NOBODY HAS PRICED — 170M+ oz Solar Demand + Export Controls = Structural Squeeze Underway
snippet: GBI Direct's analysis makes the case that China's record solar panel exports are simultaneously the largest driver of silver industrial demand and — through Beijing's January 2026 export licensing regime — a constraint on the refined silver supply that feeds non-Chinese fabricators. With China absorbing over 170 million ounces of silver annually through solar manufacturing alone, and export licensing limiting outflows to 44 approved firms, the bifurcation between where silver is consumed (China) and where it is available for Western industrial use (COMEX, LBMA) has become structural. The analysis argues that most junior silver mining equities remain priced at 2024 bear-market silver assumptions despite the January 2026 policy shift fundamentally altering the supply-demand equation — a mismatch that tends to resolve quickly when investors notice.
